text:
Jonathan Lekkerimäki has been the brightest thing about a dark Canucks season. The 15th pick of the 2022 draft has 14 points in 19 games after nine in his first 37 NHL games, and since Filip Chytil went out he has been on a line with Elias Pettersson and Brock Boeser. Canucks Army's headline put it simply: "He's got that swagger."

How much of it is real? Some. He's 0.74 points a game; the median first full season for forwards picked 10th to 20th is 0.35. But he has six goals on 3.9 expected and a 17.6% shooting percentage, so the finishing is running ahead of the chances. Vancouver has taken just 42% of the expected goals with him on the ice. He's not a burner, either: his top speed is in the bottom 11% of the league.

The good news is that wins added likes him: 48th of 504 skaters, thanks to goals that mattered. Our range has him between 42 and 68 points over a full season. Even with some cooling, this looks like a scorer who has found his level.
headline: Lekkerimäki is the bright spot
